{"self_assessment": "Impact
I took on the top line of the fish, which was the slowest stretch to build. I offered to carry it from the end of the existing run onward toward the tail, and I laid about fifteen dominoes extending it over the back. That helped it reach the tail junction so the whole fish could join up. At our final check, all 131 standing dominoes were connected to the start, and the table agreed the picture read clearly as a fish.

Execution
I worked quietly and steadily on my own stretch. I inspected the run closely early on, again mid-build, and once more near the end. These checks were to confirm that the joins on the top line were sound and that nothing was loose. When the build was complete I kept my hands off the table, because bumps were the main risk.

Collaboration
I offered to take the slow top line when I saw it was falling behind. I confirmed with Maya which end I should pick up from so we wouldn't work on top of each other. I suggested she move out toward the tail so we weren't crowding the same spot. I stayed clear of Tom's upper fork and Leo's tail work, and I offered help there if anyone wanted it. I also backed the team's decision to leave the table alone once it was finished.

Leadership
I saw where the build was bottlenecked and volunteered for it without being asked. I proposed a clear split of the work and kept the team informed about what I was doing. I supported the agreement to stop touching the table so the result would stay intact.

Overall, I contributed a real, well-placed share of the top line and helped with checking, in a team effort that produced a complete, connected fish.", "my_share_percent": 20}
